You said it. We changed it.

People who tried our prototype told us what was wrong. Here is what we did about it.

Make it small enough to carry every day.

Now a 30 mL bottle with a carabiner that clips onto your bag or keys.

Could you make a bigger version, so it lasts longer?

A 250 mL refill pump for your desk or home is in the range.

Do SPF and alcohol really work together?

They didn't, so we took SPF out to keep the formula stable and gentle.

We're registering with BPOM in Indonesia and following Australia's cosmetic rules before launch.

Before you try it

Does DermGuard treat eczema?

No. It's a cosmetic hand sanitizer made to be gentle on sensitive and eczema-prone skin. Keep using anything your doctor prescribes.

Will it sting?

It's fragrance-free and made to be gentle, but any alcohol product can sting on cracked or broken skin. That's why your first DermGuard is a free sample: test it on a small patch first.

When and where can I buy it?

We launch first in Melbourne pharmacies, then Sydney and Brisbane. Finish the quiz and we'll tell you the nearest stockist to your postcode.

DermGuard is a cosmetic hand sanitizer. It is not intended to diagnose, treat or prevent any disease. For external use only. Patch-test first and stop use if irritation occurs. Flammable: keep away from flame. Keep out of reach of children.

Privacy notice

We collect your first name, email, postcode and quiz answers to send your free sample, tell you about the launch, and decide which products to make. Answers may be summarised, without names, in our university research. We store them with our form provider, never sell them, and delete them on request. To see, correct or delete your data, or to unsubscribe, email hello@dermguard.example.
